images.caption:
Arran Heritage Museum, Rosaburn At the time of this photo the museum consisted of a group of buildings including a roadside  cottage (the white building); a smiddy (smithy) which operated from the early 19th century to the 1960s; an 18th century cottage; a milk house and a stable block.  It housed objects relating to working life on Arran together with some geological and archaeological exhibits.
Source: 1990 museum leaflet.
images.alt:
Arran Heritage Museum, Rosaburn At the time of this photo the museum consisted of a group of buildings including a roadside  cottage (the white building); a smiddy (smithy) which operated from the early 19th century to the 1960s; an 18th century cottage; a milk house and a stable block.  It housed objects relating to working life on Arran together with some geological and archaeological exhibits.
Source: 1990 museum leaflet.

images.caption: Sannox 'sheep' This iron sheep is firmly fixed to the end of the jetty at Sannox and is used as a mooring bollard. Perhaps it should be a bull with a ring through its nose, then it could be called a 'moo-ring' bollard.  Similar sheep feature at Corrie; all four harbours on this section of coast are looked after by the Corrie and Sannox Harbour Trust.

images.caption:
Circle 4 at Machrie Moor.
Four rounded granite blocks, just less than 1m high. In the middle distance on the left is the large stone of circle 3 and on the right are the three large stones of circle 2. In the far distance are the mountains of the north of Arran, consisting of Beinn Tarsuinn and Goat Fell.
